merger_description:
Bijoma North Property Pty Limited, as trustee for Bijoma North Property Unit Trust (**Bijoma Property**), and Bijoma North Operating Pty Ltd, as trustee for Bijoma North Operating Unit Trust (**Bijoma Operating**), propose to acquire the freehold interests and operating hotel businesses of Courthouse Hotel and Kinselas Hotel in Darlinghurst, NSW (the **Acquisition**). The Acquisition includes freehold land and buildings, hotel business assets, goodwill, equipment and associated liquor licence and gaming entitlements in respect of the Courthouse Hotel and Kinselas Hotel.

Bijoma Property and Bijoma Operating are entities within the Oscars Group. Oscars Group is an Australian hospitality group with a portfolio of over 40 assets across a variety of segments including pubs and gaming, accommodation, retail liquor, conference and events centres, chartered vessels, and commercial and residential developments.

The Courthouse Hotel is a pub with boutique accommodation, located at 189 Oxford Street, Darlinghurst, NSW 2010.

Kinselas Hotel is a pub and entertainment venue, located at 383 Bourke Street (Taylor Square), Darlinghurst, NSW 2010.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the increase in Oscar Group’s share of supply of dining,
function, gaming and on-premises liquor services at pub-
style venues and accommodation in the local area
surrounding the Courthouse Hotel and Kinselas Hotel is
estimated to be small
• b. there are alternative suppliers of the relevant goods and
services in the local areas surrounding the Courthouse Hotel
and Kinselas Hotel respectively.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
